raw.questionText: An ideal monoatomic gas ($C_V = \frac{3}{2}R$) undergoes various thermodynamic processes. Match the processes described in List I with their corresponding molar heat capacities in List II.
listI: 1. A process defined by the relation $T V^2 = \text{constant}$
2. A process defined by the relation $P^2 V = \text{constant}$
3. A process defined by the relation $T^2 P^{-1} = \text{constant}$
4. A process in which the work done by the gas during any infinitesimal step is related to the change in its internal energy by $dW = -2 dU$
raw.explanation: By converting non-standard process equations into the standard polytropic form $PV^n = \text{constant}$, we can directly compute the molar heat capacity using $C = C_V + \frac{R}{1-n}$.
